data.narrative:
Altara is a pre-revenue or early-stage AI & Software company founded by Eva Tuecke and Catherine Yeo. The broader AI & Software sector contains 12 identifiable peers, comprising 1 public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private firms including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. However, the company operates in a segment where traditional peer-median valuation is inapplicable due to insufficient comparable data at the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—fewer than three datapoints survive even when filtering the 12-company universe against these criteria.

The absence of a viable peer-median approach reflects the fragmentation and heterogeneity of frontier AI development. Comparable private companies in the space (Palantir's unlisted predecessors, Figure AI, Scale AI, and others) span vastly different business models, capital intensity, and maturation timelines, making stage-matched or tier-matched cohorts impractical. The single public comparable, Palantir, trades at a substantial premium to most software benchmarks but reflects a mature, profitable, and government-integrated business model largely orthogonal to early-stage AI ventures.

Without sufficient narrow-set precedent, a defensible valuation of Altara would require either (1) revenue or bookings data to anchor DCF models, (2) explicit insider pricing from recent financings, or (3) structural cost-of-capital and growth assumptions derived from first principles. The current data does not support quantitative triangulation.
